data.narrative:
Swarmbotics AI is a Seed-stage defense and security company founded by Stephen Houghton and Drew Watson that has raised $17.2M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comparable universe of 10 peers spanning public equities (2 companies) and private ventures (8 firms), including same-stage and adjacent-stage companies such as UFORCE, Anduril Industries, Helsing, Shield AI, and Saronic.

Two triangulation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis uses the $17.2M total raised as a proxy for current valuation and applies a 2.5x step-up multiplier typical for Seed-to-next-stage advancement, yielding $43M. Peer-median analysis examines five same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables with valuations ranging from $125M (NODA AI) to $4.0B (Stark Defence), producing a median of $1.0B. The peer sample includes both Seed-stage (UFORCE at $1.0B) and Series A firms (Stark Defence, Castelion, Singularity), reflecting the early-stage nature of the sector.

The triangulated range spans $37M (low) to $1.1B (high), with a median of $522M. The wide dispersion reflects substantial uncertainty in early-stage defense-tech valuations and heterogeneity within the peer set across stage and business model. The gap between stage-progression ($43M) and peer median ($1.0B) suggests either that Swarmbotics commands a discount to peer valuations at this stage, or that peer comparables skew toward better-capitalized or later-stage entrants. Key risks include technology validation, regulatory pathway clarity, and customer concentration in defense procurement.
